title: [`flake8-bugbear`] `B010`'s safe fix turns type-clean code into a type error when the attribute is a method
body:
## Summary

`B010`'s fix is classified **safe**, but when the attribute being set is a **method**, applying it turns code that type-checks cleanly into a type error. It reproduces in both `ty` and `mypy`.

`setattr(obj, "method", fn)` is a common way to install a test double over a method precisely *because* the direct assignment doesn't type-check — so the fix removes the reason the `setattr` was written.

## Reproduction

```python
class Client:
    def _call(self, method: str) -> dict:
        return {}


def test_it() -> None:
    c = Client()

    def fake(method: str) -> dict:
        return {"ok": True}

    setattr(c, "_call", fake)
```

```console
$ ruff check --select B010 --fix repro.py
Found 1 error (1 fixed, 0 remaining).
```

No `--unsafe-fixes` needed. The last line becomes `c._call = fake`.

## Result

| | `ty 0.0.80` | `mypy 2.3.1` |
|---|---|---|
| `setattr(c, "_call", fake)` — before the fix | ✅ passes | ✅ passes |
| `c._call = fake` — after the fix | ❌ `invalid-assignment` | ❌ `error: Cannot assign to a method  [method-assign]` |

```console
$ mypy repro.py            # after
repro.py:12: error: Cannot assign to a method  [method-assign]
```

## Why this bites

In a project running both `ruff --fix` and a type checker in the same pre-commit hook set, the two undo each other on every run: ruff rewrites the `setattr` into an assignment, the type checker rejects the assignment, and there is no fixed point. The only forms that satisfy both are `cast(Any, fake)` or `# type: ignore`, i.e. suppressing the checker — which is strictly worse than the `setattr`, because it also stops the checker verifying the double's signature against the real method.

Assigning over a method is a long-standing type-checking limitation ([python/mypy#2427](https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/2427), open since 2016; [mypy's docs](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/common_issues.html) suggest `Any` or `type: ignore`), so `setattr` is a natural escape and the rule removes it.

## Suggested resolution

Any of:

1. Don't flag `B010` when the attribute name resolves to a method on the target's type.
2. Keep the diagnostic, mark the fix **unsafe** in that case — matching the precedent in [#22657](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/pull/22657), where `B010`'s fix was made unsafe because it could delete comments.
3. Mark the fix unsafe whenever the assigned value is a callable.

(2) seems the smallest change consistent with existing behaviour.

## Version

`ruff 0.16.6`, `ty 0.0.80`, `mypy 2.3.1`, Python 3.13/3.14, macOS arm64.
